✦ Deep Dives

Mental Health Articles

Understanding common issues and evidence-based coping strategies to move forward.

Anxiety

Understanding Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD)

GAD is characterized by persistent, excessive worry about everyday matters. It affects ~3% of adults globally and often co-exists with depression. Recognizing triggers is the first step to relief.

  • Practice diaphragmatic breathing (4-7-8 technique)
  • Cognitive restructuring: challenge "what-if" thoughts
  • Schedule 15 min "worry time" to contain anxious thoughts
  • Regular aerobic exercise reduces cortisol levels
Depression

Navigating Clinical Depression

More than sadness, depression is a medical condition involving persistent low mood, loss of interest, and physical symptoms. It is highly treatable with therapy, medication, or both.

  • Behavioral activation: do small activities even without motivation
  • Maintain consistent sleep and wake times
  • Seek social connection even when it feels hard
  • CBT or DBT therapy has strong evidence for depression
Stress

Chronic Stress and Your Body

Prolonged stress triggers the HPA axis, flooding the body with cortisol. Over time this damages cardiovascular health, immunity, and memory. The good news: the stress response is trainable.

  • Progressive muscle relaxation (PMR) before bed
  • Time-blocking your day to reduce decision fatigue
  • Nature walks lower cortisol measurably within 20 minutes
  • Journaling helps offload cognitive load
Sleep Disorders

Insomnia: When Sleep Becomes a Battle

Insomnia affects 1 in 3 adults. Poor sleep worsens anxiety, depression, and cognitive function. CBT for Insomnia (CBT-I) is proven to outperform sleep medications long-term.

  • Keep a fixed sleep/wake schedule 7 days a week
  • Stimulus control: bed is only for sleep and intimacy
  • Avoid screens 1 hour before bed; dim lights at night
  • Try sleep restriction therapy with a professional
Mindfulness

The Science of Mindfulness Meditation

Mindfulness restructures the prefrontal cortex and shrinks the amygdala after just 8 weeks of practice (MBSR research). It reduces anxiety, depression relapse, and chronic pain perception.

  • Start with 5 minutes of breath-focused meditation daily
  • Body scan practice to reconnect with physical sensations
  • MBSR (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction) 8-week program
  • Non-judgmental awareness throughout daily activities
Grief

Grief: Moving Through Loss Without "Getting Over It"

Grief is not linear. The Dual Process Model shows healthy grieving alternates between confronting loss and engaging in life. Complicated grief affects 10-15% of bereaved people and needs support.

  • Allow yourself to feel grief in waves, without judgment
  • Create rituals of remembrance that feel meaningful
  • Connect with grief support groups (in-person or online)
  • Avoid major life decisions in the acute grief phase
Burnout

Workplace Burnout: Exhaustion Is Not a Badge of Honor

Burnout is an official WHO diagnosis involving emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced efficacy. It's caused by chronic workplace stress that hasn't been successfully managed.

  • Set non-negotiable work boundaries (no emails after 7pm)
  • Identify your core values and align work accordingly
  • Take micro-recovery breaks every 90 minutes
  • Consider job crafting or a role change if values misalign
Self-Esteem

Low Self-Esteem: Rewiring Your Inner Critic

Low self-esteem often originates in childhood experiences and is maintained by cognitive distortions. It predicts depression, anxiety, and relationship difficulties throughout life.

  • Identify and name your inner critic — separate it from "you"
  • Self-compassion practice (Dr. Kristin Neff's method)
  • Keep a daily "evidence log" of your accomplishments
  • Challenge comparisons by listing your unique strengths
Loneliness

The Loneliness Epidemic and How to Combat It

Loneliness is as dangerous as smoking 15 cigarettes a day (Holt-Lunstad, 2015). It triggers inflammatory responses and is rising across all age groups in the modern world.

  • Seek quality over quantity in relationships
  • Volunteer or join a community group around shared interests
  • Practice vulnerability: share something real with someone safe
  • Limit passive social media scrolling; use it actively instead
Trauma & PTSD

Healing from Trauma: Understanding the Nervous System

Trauma lives in the body. Bessel van der Kolk's research shows trauma disrupts the brain's threat response. Healing requires bottom-up approaches, not just talking alone.

  • Somatic experiencing: track body sensations safely
  • EMDR therapy is FDA-approved for PTSD treatment
  • Co-regulation with safe, attuned relationships
  • Trauma-sensitive yoga and breath practices
Anger Management

Anger Is Not the Enemy — Mismanaged Anger Is

Anger is a signal, not a flaw. It indicates a boundary has been crossed or a need isn't being met. The goal isn't to suppress anger but to express it constructively and understand its source.

  • The STOP skill: Stop, Take a breath, Observe, Proceed
  • Physical exercise as a legitimate release valve
  • Delay response by 10 minutes during heated moments
  • Assert needs with "I feel…when…because…I need…" framework
OCD

OCD: Beyond Stereotypes to Real Understanding

OCD is not just about cleanliness. It involves intrusive thoughts and compulsions used to neutralize anxiety. ERP (Exposure and Response Prevention) is the gold standard treatment.

  • ERP therapy: expose to feared stimuli without compulsions
  • Accept intrusive thoughts as "just noise" — don't engage
  • Mindfulness to observe thoughts without fusing with them
  • Medication (SSRIs) combined with ERP shows best outcomes
Social Anxiety

Social Anxiety: More Than Just Shyness

Social anxiety disorder (SAD) is the 3rd most common mental health issue globally. It involves intense fear of social situations and scrutiny, leading to significant avoidance and impairment.

  • Gradual exposure hierarchy: from least to most feared situations
  • Attention training: shift focus from self-monitoring to surroundings
  • Challenge post-event processing (replaying embarrassment)
  • Social skills practice in low-stakes environments
Emotional Regulation

Emotional Regulation: The Core Skill Nobody Taught Us

Emotional dysregulation underlies most mental health conditions. DBT (Dialectical Behavior Therapy) developed by Dr. Marsha Linehan offers a comprehensive skill set for managing intense emotions.

  • TIPP: Temperature, Intense exercise, Paced breathing, Paired muscle relaxation
  • Opposite action: act opposite to emotion's urge
  • Check the facts before acting on intense feelings
  • Build positive experiences intentionally each day
Seasonal Affective Disorder

Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) — When Seasons Shift Your Mood

SAD affects ~5% of adults, triggered by reduced sunlight disrupting circadian rhythms and serotonin levels. Most common in autumn/winter and especially prevalent in higher latitudes.

  • Light therapy (10,000 lux) for 20-30 min each morning
  • Maintain regular outdoor time even on cloudy days
  • Vitamin D supplementation (consult your doctor)
  • Keep social and physical activity routines through winter
